text:
anya: Quick heads-up from bring-up of 'astra-lite-6b' (converted from gemma-format) — after an int4 pass the model looks fine on short prompts but begins to degenerate into repetitive tokens around ~1k tokens. suspect rotary frequency scaling + tokenizer normalization interaction. attaching quick diffs.
devon: can you paste the failing prompt + the short/long rollout metrics? also which conversion tool/version?
anya: conversion: tools/convert-gemma-to-redwood v0.9.3. sample prompt below and perplexity delta:
```
Prompt: "Write a long technical analysis of progressive quantization strategies..."
Short (<=128): ppl 12.4
Long (~2048): ppl 48.1, repetition spikes after 1024
```
liam: ugh. that pattern screams rotary mismatch (freq scale) across head groups — if headwise scaling got applied differently during conversion we see prefix coherence collapse. did convert script run any headwise rescale heuristic?
anya: yes, convert script applied a "shim_layer" with per-head scale factor to approximate gemma->qwen rotaries (quick hack). code snippet:
```
# conv shim
for h in range(n_heads):
    scale[h] = base_scale * (1 - 0.02 * (h / n_heads))
```
We didn't think it'd affect longctx that badly.
maya: worth checking tokenizer too — the tokenizer normalizer appears to strip soft hyphens (U+00AD) and also collapses some combining diacritics. If token offsets shift, kv-cache alignment could be off after long prefixes and interact poorly with rotary. run tokenizer.debug on the long prompt.
devon: good call. anya can you run tokenization diffs: original gemma tokenizer vs converted tokenizer on the same plaintext? if tokens misalign that's a red flag.
anya: ran it — there are ~0.8% token index shifts on long document because of soft-hyphen + zero-width joiner handling. sample diff attached (snippet):
```
orig: [ ... 1021:'word', 1022:'\u00AD', 1023:'suffix' ]
conv: [ ... 1021:'word\u00AD', 1022:'suffix' ]
```
liam: that combined with a per-head rotary shim is a plausible 2-factor failure mode. Token shifts change positional queries to kv-cache mapping; if rotary freq is also headwise-warped the attention pattern decays.
onboard-bot: Dedicated repro instance spun up: ded-ast-03 (GPU: a100-80g), link: http://infra/internal/ded-ast-03 — logs and eval harness queued.
maya: thanks. I'll run tokenization-only regression across a handful of long documents and dump token offsets.
devon: meanwhile try a quick ablation: 1) disable shim_layer (use uniform scale=1.0) 2) keep converted tokenizer 3) run longctx eval. that'll tell us if shim is primary.
anya: started ablation job on ded-ast-03: queued job id 17855501. ETA ~8m.
liam: also try a soft patch — align tokenization by reapplying NFKC normalization that gemma used before conversion. if that reduces offsets then it's tokenizer-fixable.
ops: allocated extra storage for the eval artifacts, ETA 2m.
anya: quick update: ablation 1 (shim disabled) dropped the longctx ppl from 48.1 -> 18.7, repetition disappeared in the sample. so shim is the main culprit.
maya: interesting — so shim heuristic introduced a harmful headwise warp. we should revert to a deterministic mapping and compute analytical freq rescale from model dims rather than a linear headwise fudge.
liam: agreed. plan: revert shim, compute freq_table using canonical formula used by gemma: freq = base * (head_multiplier**(head_index)) then match by fitting to original checkpoints (small L2 fit). no per-head ad-hoc slope.
devon: also open PR to add tokenizer compatibility tests in onboarding harness: token index parity for 2k-window documents. if that fails, conversion should abort or emit a warning.
anya: creating issue and PR: #onboard/ast-rotary-shim-fix. will push the revert + recalculated freq_table and re-run quant with int4 per-channel scaling ON and OFF just to be safe.
onboard-bot: job 17855501 completed: logs attached -> https://artifacts.internal/17855501 — summary: shim off yields baseline-like behavior.
maya: great. follow-ups: (1) full bisect to see when shim was introduced, (2) update convert tool with deterministic freq estimator + opt-in headwise scaling, (3) add token parity check as gating, (4) run scheduled eval suite on dedicated for 24h to catch slow regressions.
ops: I've added a 24h run on ded-ast-03, scheduled start in 10m.
liam: note for the conversion doc: call out soft-hyphen and ZWJ differences between tokenizers explicitly and provide a normalization toggle. also document that headwise scaling is opt-in and experimental.
anya: thanks all — will file the PRs and post back with final numbers. :thumbsup:
